svg.title: Job expansion: the loop in Plan(), step by step
svg.desc: Three pending jobs. Each row shows the code that runs for one loop iteration and the three containers after it. The last row shows how job_index is used when the response is built.

text.font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'DejaVu Sans Mono', monospace

g.text: Then, for every entry of plan_ctx->scheduled_jobs: node_indices = positions of its ActionNodes, state = STATE_EXECUTING (RETRIEVE also gets bay_id), and it is appended to result.scheduled_jobs.

text.font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: Final result.scheduled_jobs = [INSERT STATE_ERROR, RETRIEVE STATE_EXECUTING, REPARK_TRAY STATE_EXECUTING]: failures first, in loop order, then successes.

text.font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: Why size() and not i: the index must point into scheduled_jobs, which only holds successful jobs. With i, the REPARK's events would say 2 and scheduled_jobs[2] does not exist.

text.font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'DejaVu Sans Mono', monospace

g.text: Job expansion: the loop in Plan(), step by step

text.font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: job_index is not the job's position in the request (i). It is its position in plan_ctx->scheduled_jobs, the list of jobs that have succeeded so far, and that list is what the response uses to map

text.font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
